sentence_stem: By the time the train arrives tomorrow morning,
correct_completion: we will have been waiting on the platform for over three hours.
full_sentence: By the time the train arrives tomorrow morning, we will have been waiting on the platform for over three hours.
acceptable_variants: we will have been standing here for hours.
we will have spent hours waiting for it.

options.text: we waited on the platform for three hours yesterday.
options.why_wrong: This is a past simple statement. It does not describe a duration that will be completed by a future point in time, as the 'by the time' clause requires.

options.text: we are going to wait for the next train.
options.why_wrong: This expresses a future plan rather than a duration that will be complete before a future moment, so it does not match the 'by the time' structure.

options.text: we will have been waiting on the platform for over three hours.
we have been waiting since morning.
options.why_wrong: This is a present perfect continuous structure. It refers to the past up to now, not to a future moment, so it does not fit the 'by the time' clause.

grammar_focus: Future perfect continuous with 'by the time' clauses
explanation: The future perfect continuous describes an action that will still be in progress up to a point in the future. That point is set here by the 'by the time' clause with a present-tense verb referring to the future. Learners often use a simple future tense in this situation because their first language has no separate perfect tense, so the duration nuance is easy to miss.
translation: Do chwili, gdy pociąg przyjedzie jutro rano, będziemy czekać na peronie już ponad trzy godziny.
